h: פָּרָשַׁת זָכוֹר, מַאֲמָר י׳ Parshas Zachor — Maamar Yud

p: "Hashem maintains a war against Amalek from generation to generation."
until the generation of Mordechai and Esther;
from the generation of Mordechai and Esther
is that three times we find
the matter of the eradication of Amalek:
when Amalek attached himself to them
for he only weakened his strength.
And in the generation of Mordechai and Esther
and sought to destroy, to kill and to annihilate,
they over those who hated them" (Esther 9:1).
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל שְׁמוּאֵל
This was not so in the generation of Shmuel,
when we do not find at all
to utterly destroy all that belonged to Amalek
The explanation is that in the wilderness,
for the revelation of the Written Torah,
they slackened themselves from words of Torah
and this came about through Amalek,
slackness of hands from words of Torah,
that through the giving of the Torah
וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּל הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע
and this is through the nullification of the yetzer hara,
וְהוּא מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת הוּא יֵצֶר הָרָע
and the Angel of Death is the yetzer hara
and Amalek is the evil inclination,
as they said in the holy Zohar
And so too in the generation of Mordechai and Esther,
of the Men of the Great Assembly,
"Ezra came up from Bavel and established it";
וְעַל כֵּן הִתְגָּרָה עֲמָלֵק גַּם כֵּן
for through this there was then established
"they accepted it anew in the days of Achashverosh";
for it was about this that there was
the holding of the mountain over them like a barrel,
they said, "We will do and we will hear"
And so it is written after the eradication of Amalek,
which is called "orah" in the feminine,
for it receives from the Written Torah,
And in the generation of Moshe, when they were in the wilderness
for the complete eradication of Amalek,
"And it shall be, when Hashem gives rest," etc.,
"in the land that Hashem your God
gives you as an inheritance to possess,
However, in the generation of Shmuel,
Amalek did not then provoke Yisrael,
but since they were in Eretz Yisrael,
to utterly destroy all that belonged to Amalek.
הָיָה אָז מְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק מִכֹּל וָכֹל
there would then have been the complete eradication of Amalek
who is of the seed of Binyamin,
and through him too it was fitting there be
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [שׁוֹפְטִים ה, יד] אַחֲרֶיךָ בִנְיָמִין
as it is said (Shoftim 5:14), "After you, Binyamin,"
and they said on this in the Pesikta
to exact retribution from the seed of Amalek."
וְאָז הָיָה דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And then David HaMelech, alav hashalom,
and Shaul was fit to be
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר יְהוֹנָתָן [שְׁמוּאֵל א כג, יז]
"And I shall be second to you."
רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהִשְׁאִיר שָׁאוּל אֶת אֲגַג
But because Shaul left Agag alive,
and through this he provoked Yisrael
in the generation of Mordechai and Esther,
for the revelation of Torah she'b'al peh,
and then there was the eradication of Amalek
And Torah she'b'al peh was established,
as they said, "they accepted it anew," etc.,
But the main revelation of Torah she'b'al peh
will be in the time of Mashiach ben David,
"The Torah that a person learns in this world
compared to the Torah of Mashiach."
And then will be the main eradication of Amalek,
on the part of Hashem Yisbarach.
And this is the root of their dispute:
for then it was fitting that there be
the command of Shmuel from the mouth of Hashem,
"Hashem maintains a war against Amalek from generation to generation"
was said after the war with Amalek,
the generation of Moshe is not counted
within what is said, "from generation to generation,"
but only from the generation of Shmuel
until the generation of Mordechai and Esther,
that from now there will be the generation of Shmuel,
in which Hashem Yisbarach will begin, on His part,
to carry out the eradication of Amalek,
and it will not be completed,
for afterwards Amalek will awaken again
in the generation of Mordechai and Esther.
from the generation of Mordechai and Esther, etc.,
for he did not count the generation of Shmuel,
since there was no proper eradication.
For Shaul spoiled it by leaving Agag,
and he counted as the beginning
to nullify the revelation of Torah she'b'al peh
and then there was the eradication of Amalek,
and they accepted Torah she'b'al peh,
when there will be the main revelation
as we said from the Midrash,
and then will be the main eradication of Amalek;
and on this he brings the exposition
דְּדוֹרוֹ שֶׁל מָשִׁיחַ הוּא שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת
that the generation of Mashiach is three generations,
as it is written, "And before the moon, dor dorim":
alluding that the generation of Mashiach
in which there was eradication of Amalek:
in which it came from Hashem Yisbarach's side,
who commanded to destroy his memory.
Yisrael will sense a renewed taste
and then the eradication of Amalek will be twofold:
and also from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
as in the three generations mentioned above.
And regarding this Yisrael were commanded,
"You shall erase the memory of Amalek."
And it is found (Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 4):
we are not able to overcome him."
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to them,
and I will erase his name from Above," etc.
And this is what is said, "Do not forget":
that at the very least you must not forget
to erase the memory of Amalek,
and then Hashem Yisbarach erases his name
And for this purpose comes the reading of the parsha:
that He erase the name of Amalek from Above;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה נִזְכֶּה לִמְחִיַּית עֲמָלֵק
and through this we will merit the eradication of Amalek
who will destroy his memory completely,
speedily in our days, amen selah.

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma, Ki Seitzei 11 — “‘From generation to generation.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I pursue him through every generation. Rabbi Eliezer says: From the generation of Moshe until that of Shmuel. Rabbi Yehoshua says: From the generation of Shmuel until that of Mordechai and Esther. Rabbi Yosei says: From the generation of Mordechai and Esther until the King Mashiach, which is three generations. From where is the generation of Mashiach three generations? ‘They will fear You with the sun, and before the moon, generation of generations’: dor is one, dorim are two, making three.” The text’s count is a derashah on Tehillim 72:5, rather than a conventional three-generation chronology. Rav Tzadok explains how the messianic generation contains the three stages of confrontation with Amalek.

paragraphs.text: Shemos Rabbah 41:7 — “‘Engraved upon the tablets’—what is charus? Rabbi Yehudah says: Do not read charus, engraved, but cheirus, freedom from exile. Rabbi Nechemiah says: Freedom from the Angel of Death. The Sages say: Freedom from suffering. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said: If the Angel of Death says before the Holy One, blessed be He, ‘You created me in the world for nothing,’ He answers: I gave you dominion over every nation in the world, except this nation, to which I gave freedom.” Freedom from death is one of the Midrash’s interpretations of the tablets. Rav Tzadok explains why Amalek’s opposition to Torah therefore threatens the persistence of the evil inclination itself.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Machshavos Charutz 17 — “He thought that since Moshe died in Adar the Torah’s influence ceased; he did not know that Moshe was also born in Adar… and his decree prepared for ‘they accepted it anew.’” Rav Tzadok there explains why Haman’s attack on the Torah turned into its renewal. Yisrael stand above time and determine what a season is ready for.

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbati 13:4 — “What is ‘After you, Binyamin’? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Forever after you, Binyamin, to exact payment from Amalek’s offspring. Know that a man from Amalek’s offspring arose against Israel, and none stood against him except one from Binyamin’s offspring. Who was this? Haman the wicked. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: By your life, a man from Binyamin’s offspring is prepared to uproot your roots. Who was this? Mordechai, as it says, ‘A Jewish man was in Shushan the capital, named Mordechai ... a Benjaminite.’” The preceding exposition also cites Yehoshua, of Ephraim, as a descendant of Rachel who fought Amalek. Thus the source supplies the Rachel–Yosef–Binyamin pattern developed here.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Poked Akarim 5 — “The first of the soul of Mashiach ben Yosef revealed in this world, it seems to me, was Yonasan ben Shaul… as I saw in Asarah Maamaros on ‘And I shall be second to you.’” Rav Tzadok there fills out the picture: Shaul’s kingship, which preceded David’s, was like Eliyahu’s coming before ben David. Free of sin and given rest from evil, Shaul was charged with uprooting Amalek’s very root.

paragraphs.text: Kohelet Rabbah 11:8 — “‘If a person lives many years’—let him rejoice in the joy of Torah. ‘Let him remember the days of darkness’—these are the days of adversity. ‘For they will be many’: The Torah a person learns in this world is vapor before the Torah of Mashiach.” The comparison expresses the vastness of the future disclosure. Rav Tzadok connects that new light in both modes of Torah with the final removal of Amalek.
